name: anyquery
why: Runs SQL across many external sources like apps and APIs, a fun door into treating everything as a database.

brief.what_it_is: Anyquery is a SQL query engine, built on SQLite, that exposes apps, files, and databases as tables you can query with one dialect. Its sources include GitHub, Notion, Spotify, Gmail, Airtable, Google Sheets, Apple Notes, Chrome, Todoist, CSV and Parquet files, and logs, with 40+ in total via plugins. It takes SQL in through a shell, through a MySQL-protocol server, or through an MCP server for LLM clients, and returns rows from the underlying services. It also supports INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE on some sources such as Notion, Airtable, and Google Sheets.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage pitches it as one way to ask questions of everything you already use, so you don't have to learn the Notion API, write a Gmail scraper, or install four CLI tools. The README frames it as a SQL query engine that can run queries on pretty much anything.
brief.how_it_works: Anyquery runs on SQLite and uses plugins to turn each external service or file type into a table, so you can JOIN across them. It runs locally and the homepage says API tokens never leave the machine. It can run as an MCP server so LLM clients can query your data, or as a MySQL-compatible server so tools like Metabase and TablePlus can connect.

commands_seen.cmd: CGO_ENABLED=1 go install -tags "vtable fts5 sqlite_json sqlite_math_functions" github.com/julien040/anyquery@main
commands_seen.context: Builds from source with Go, requiring Go 1.26+ and a C compiler because of go-sqlite3 cgo.

brief.install_notes: Beyond brew, the README lists a quick install script (curl ... | sh), AUR (yay -S anyquery-git or paru -S anyquery-git), APT and YUM/DNF repos hosted by the author, Scoop, Winget (winget install JulienCagniart.anyquery), Chocolatey, and direct binaries from the GitHub releases page. Building from source needs Go 1.26+ and a C compiler (gcc, clang, or mingw on Windows) on PATH. Plugins are installed separately with anyquery i followed by names, and the README says any SQLite extension can be loaded too. No accounts are mentioned for the core engine, though some plugins will need their own API tokens.
brief.standout: Most tools in this space cover one source; this one puts 40+ apps, files, and databases behind a single SQLite dialect, with JOINs across them, and writes back to some of them. It also ships as an MCP server with one command, so an LLM can answer questions by running real SQL against your own accounts.
brief.status: Appears maintained but the signals are mixed. The README badges show commit activity and an issues tracker, and the install script example references version 0.4.5, while a Go reference badge points at v0.1.3. The homepage says it is built and maintained by one person. I did not find a release date or last-commit date in the pages I read, so the exact recency is unknown.
brief.caveats: The core engine is AGPL-3.0, while the RPC library is MIT and each plugin has its own license, so check plugin terms before reuse. Building from source needs Go 1.26+ and cgo with a C toolchain. The README says it is built and maintained by one person, and it currently accepts only minor contributions. The homepage and README both carry sponsor banners, and the homepage also carries a personal internship-seeking notice from the author. The README's license link points to an 'anquery' path, which looks like a typo. Windows is supported through Scoop, Winget, or Chocolatey rather than the shell script. The homepage's own claims are marketing copy, and the sample Spotify conversation is marked as illustrative.
quotes: One binary, one dialect, one way of asking questions.
You write SELECT and Anyquery does the rest — across 40+ services and every file on disk.
Anyquery is built and maintained by one person. Sponsoring keeps it free and open-source.
